mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the same month indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous month - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals a contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month - 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not negative in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase of more than 0.3 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a decline of more than 2% in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a synchronized weakening of labor and production, which raises recession probability and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > previous month + 0.3pp AND INDPRO < previous month - 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 2% for two consecutive months signals an accommodative monetary policy stance, lowering risk-free rates and increasing present value of future cash flows, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 alongside a concurrent decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and reduces profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase of more than 0.2% in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1, quarter-over-quarter annualized) signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and earnings expectations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered quarters.
